study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Maximum intrapartum temperature: afebrile (<38°C), mild fever (38°C-39°C), and severe fever (>39°C)
Duration from reaching maximum temperature to delivery
outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (umbilical artery pH <7.1, mechanical ventilation, respiratory distress, meconium aspiration with pulmonary hypertension, hypoglycemia, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and Apgar <7 at 5 minutes)
Composite neonatal neurologic morbidity (hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, hypothermia treatment, and seizures)
Composite maternal morbidity (postpartum hemorrhage, endometritis, and maternal packed red blood cell transfusion)
cohort: 8132 term, singleton pregnancies admitted for induction of labor or spontaneous labor who had intrapartum fever (≥38°C)
finding: Composite neonatal morbidity increased with intrapartum fever severity, independent of the duration from reaching maximum intrapartum temperature to delivery.
mod_finding: This study found that composite neonatal morbidity correlated with intrapartum fever severity, and this correlation was independent of the duration from reaching maximum intrapartum temperature to delivery, suggesting that the timing or mode of delivery should not be affected by this duration.
